findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)'. The Cisco ACI add-on was TA_cisco-ACI (1897), now archived in favour of Cisco DC Networking (7777). The wrong ID also appears in implementation, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Point to Cisco DC Networking (cisco_dc_networking_app_for_splunk, Splunkbase 7777) for APIC API collection, note TA_cisco-ACI (1897) as deprecated, and remove the 4022 references.

findings.explanation: APIC faultInst carries its own `domain` attribute (Cisco's examples show `access` and `infra`; a node-unreachable fault under topology/ is domain `infra`, not `fabric`). The SPL prefers the vendor value when it is present and falls back to these DN-regex labels otherwise, so 'fabric' and 'mgmt' buckets can sit beside vendor values such as 'infra' and 'management' for the same kind of fault.
findings.quote: `case` mirrors **APIC** fault domains: `tenant` when **`dn`** references `/tn-`, `fabric` for `topology/` / routing classes, `access` for `phys` / port classes, `infra` for `infra/` / policy plumbing, `mgmt` for aaa users
findings.suggested_fix: Check the APIC MIM enumeration for faultInst.domain and make the fallback labels use exactly the vendor vocabulary. Drop the claim that the regex 'mirrors APIC fault domains' unless they match.

findings.explanation: Cisco models delegates as a separate class (faultDelegate, a copy of faultInst attached to a more visible MO), not as faultInst rows carrying a 'delegated' flag. If faultDelegate is pulled into the same sourcetype, as dataSources allows, the filter keeps those rows because `delegated_f` defaults to 'no'.
findings.quote: the **`delegated`** filter drops parent bubble rows that would double-count fabric defects
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether the collected JSON has a `delegated` attribute. If it does not, dedupe by excluding the faultDelegate class (via a class or moClass field) instead of a delegated flag.

findings.explanation: The alert condition contains a broken field name ('af fected_mos') and refers to `health_feed_ok`, which the SPL never produces (it outputs health_feed_alive). The 25 and 40 thresholds appear nowhere in the SPL, description or implementation, and implementation says 'hourly rollups' while this section schedules every 15 minutes.
findings.quote: custom condition `search af fected_mos > 25 AND sev IN ("critical","major") AND fault_domain!="unknown"` for sev-2, tighten to >40 for sev-1 ... `health_feed_ok`
findings.suggested_fix: Write the condition as `affected_mos > 25 AND sev IN ("critical","major") AND fault_domain!="unknown"`, use health_feed_alive, and state one schedule and one set of thresholds in implementation, description and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The left joins only set `*_feed_alive=1` when a feed returns an event. A dead feed leaves the field null, never 0, so a panel looking for 0 will not light up.
findings.quote: a 0 tells you the rollup may be blind due to collector outages
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the flag is blank or null for a silent feed, or tell the reader to add `fillnull value=0` on the four flags.

findings.explanation: The 'Faults, Events, and System Messages Management Guide' and 'Object Model Reference — faultInst' entries link to the cisco.com and developer.cisco.com home pages, not to the named documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the faults guide at https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/datacenter/aci/apic/sw/all/faults/guide/b_APIC_Faults_Errors/b_IFC_Faults_Errors_chapter_01.html and the APIC MIM faultInst page for the release in use.

findings.explanation: The SPL never counts or correlates aaaModLR change records. The audit sourcetype only sets a feed-alive flag, so the Change model claim is not supported by the detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Alerts and drop Change, or describe Change as an optional enrichment that is not part of the shipped search.

findings.explanation: An automated agent did the review ('agent-handcraft-2026-04-29'), and the UC still has a wrong add-on ID and placeholder references, so the verified status is not supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME validates the add-on, the fields and the domain mapping.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `stats ... max(len(code_u)) as code_width` is invalid. stats aggregations accept a field name or an `eval(...)` expression, so this needs `max(eval(len(code_u)))`, or a prior `eval code_len=len(code_u)`. As written the search errors out. code_width is also never used in the final table.
`sort fault_domain -affected_mos -sev` sorts severity alphabetically (warning > minor > major > critical), not by severity rank. Add a numeric severity rank if the ordering is meant to be meaningful.

summary: The fault-domain rollup idea and the lifecycle and delegation reasoning are sound, but the add-on ID is wrong, the SPL contains an invalid stats aggregation, and the domain buckets, feed-alive semantics and alert thresholds in the prose do not match the search. Two of the references are bare vendor landing URLs.
